claim: A diagnosis is a minimal hitting set of the conflict sets; a conflict is a set of components that cannot all be normal given the model and the observation. A claimed conflict can be checked mechanically.
agent_test: Have the model propose conflicts; a code check confirms each is violated; compare diagnosis quality to free-form hypothesis lists at equal tokens.

claim: New measurements can ADD diagnoses (strict supersets of rejected ones), and diagnosis is nonmonotonic. A scaffold must not treat elimination as monotone.
agent_test: Plant a task where one probe both kills and creates candidates; check the agent keeps a set and re-derives it rather than pruning one-way.

claim: Reiter's original hitting-set tree can miss minimal hitting sets: the edge-pruning rule can delete a node that a closing rule relied on, especially with non-minimal conflict sets. Greiner, Smith and Wilkerson (1989) repaired it with HS-DAG and a correctness proof. Model-written or old hitting-set code needs checking against a vetted solver.
agent_test: Ask the model to write a hitting-set routine; compare with a reference solver on random conflict families.
note_d: Greiner 1989 opened this run (d01, d02); Reiter 1987 original read earlier from OCR (a02-a05). Two papers, one is the correction of the other, so the count is generous.

claim: For the hitting-set step, vetted solvers (MMCS, RS, HTC-BDD) are far faster than classic diagnosis algorithms; some published implementations had errors.
agent_test: Call a solver tool vs let the model enumerate; compare correctness and tokens.

claim: Pooling many failing observations and hitting their conflicts together scales; diagnosing each failure alone or merging all into one formula does not.
agent_test: With 5-10 failing checks, compare pooled conflict sets vs per-failure diagnosis at equal tokens.

claim: Greedy stochastic or preferred-first search with conflicts finds a good diagnosis where exact complete methods time out (SAFARI 100% on all ISCAS85 tests vs CDA 0-74%, HA 1-71%).
agent_test: Anytime search with token budget vs exhaustive hypothesis listing.

claim: Fault-model choice matters: weak-fault models (no modelling of abnormal behaviour) are far easier to search; strong-fault models degrade quality on large circuits.
agent_test: Compare agent with weak vs strong fault assumptions on tasks with unknown failure modes.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs do not replace diagnosis algorithms: o3-mini conflicts F1 0.917 +/-0.249, diagnoses F1 0.784 +/-0.322, falling as diagnoses grow (up to 165); gpt-4o-mini incidence matrix F1 0.47, accuracy 0.00.
agent_test: Replicate on a different circuit family and non-OpenAI models; one paper only, OpenAI models only.

claim: More domain knowledge in the prompt, or handing over the correct incidence matrix, did not improve MSO generation; model strength and tools mattered more.
agent_test: Equal-token test: rich MBD primer vs bare task on conflict generation.

claim: Describing a diagnostic algorithm in the prompt does not make a model follow it; moving state and traversal into a deterministic controller does (EoG maj@3 F1 86.1 vs ReAct 8.6 for GPT-5.1, 35 scenarios).
agent_test: Same agent with algorithm in prompt vs external state/controller, equal tokens; report majority@k.

claim: Pass@k overstates reliability of diagnosis agents; majority@k is much lower (Gemini 3 Flash 89% pass vs 74% majority; ReAct GPT-OSS-120B 5.7% maj@3 F1).
agent_test: Report majority@k not pass@k for every diagnosis test.

claim: Free-form agents are poor at real multi-component diagnosis: ITBench SRE gpt-4o pass@1 13.81% (Table 4) or 18.10% (Table 19); OpenRCA perfect detection 3.9-12.5%.
agent_test: Use as baseline difficulty; replicate on an in-house incident set.

claim: Common failures: hallucinated interpretation (71.2% of runs), incomplete exploration (63.9%), Symptom-as-Cause (39.9%), No Cross-Validation (18.6%); prompt-level pitfall warnings did not fix them, richer error output did.
agent_test: Add an explicit alternative-explanation check and compare Symptom-as-Cause rate; failure coding was LLM-assisted.

claim: Locating the faulty step is the hard part for LLMs; correction given the true location works. GPT-4 52.87 location accuracy on BIG-Bench Mistake; a 60-70% accurate locator is enough for backtracking to help.
agent_test: Pair an external locator (code check, test) with model repair and compare to self-judged location.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8 after two rounds).
agent_test: Revision only on a failing check vs always-reflect, equal tokens.
note_d: 2025-26 evidence: CorrectBench finds reasoning models gain little from added correction (d06); Li finds the strongest model (94%) corrects 16.7% of its errors vs 26.8% for GPT-3.5 and that location hints hurt (d07). Not yet tested on diagnosis tasks with a reasoning model, so no change of status.

claim: Real execution output is the strongest localisation signal: removing the error log cut ChatGPT-4 Top-1 by 25.6%; simulated debugger output reduced AutoSD reliability (plausible 73% real vs 63% ablated).
agent_test: Run candidate-test steps through real tools vs model-imagined results.

claim: LLM localisation collapses with large context (class-level 49.9% worse than SmartFL) and a weak model gives good top-1 but poor top-3/5.
agent_test: Feed small slices vs whole context at equal tokens.

claim: LLM explanations of a fault are often wrong even when the location is right (about 20% of 300 explanations accurate); agreement across runs correlates with correctness but is only a ranking hint.
agent_test: Check whether agreement-rank beats a verifier-rank at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Model size drives diagnosis quality and hallucination of non-existent components (hit rate 79.5% down to 0%; hallucination 7.7-20.5% for the top three vs over 70% for most small models). Only 1 of 13 models named a valid double fault.
agent_test: Test whether a candidate-exists check and a prompt forcing multi-fault candidates fix the double-fault omission.

claim: Familiar textbook circuits inflate scores (Phi-2 appended textbook Exercise sections; ChatGPT solved the classic bulb circuit); novel topologies are the proper probe.
agent_test: Use unfamiliar topologies and renamed components in tests.

claim: Where an LLM sits on top of a consistency-based engine and only explains/labels, results look good but evidence is mostly single demonstrations (PRO-AID sensor bias case; FLEX F1 0.99).
agent_test: Compare LLM-as-reasoner vs LLM-as-interface on the same task. Evidence is anecdotal, no ablations.
note_d: d09 (SDBench) shows structured hypothesis tracking plus a challenger and cost steward helps cost-efficiency; no per-role ablation, so still contested.

claim: Accept-only-if-better revision loops and diagnosis-guided repair lift scores (TN-AutoRCA F1 58.99 to 91.79; HypoAgent ablations), but on benchmark-tuned setups.
agent_test: Test whether accept-if-explains-more beats unconditional revision on held-out items; generalisation unshown.

claim: Belief revision (retracting earlier cause/symptom labels on new evidence) adds measurable gain, mostly for weaker models (+6.9% to +64.3% relative maj@3 recall).
agent_test: Ablate retraction in the agent loop.

claim: No published test was found of an LLM generating conflicts inside a Reiter hitting-set loop with next-probe choice on the classic benchmark circuits (searches were rate-limited).
agent_test: Run our own benchmark; verify absence with a better literature search.
note_d: Gap search repeated with OpenAlex, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, web search: still no published test (d04). Absence is probable, not certain, since arXiv API returned empty.

claim: A code-scored next-test choice (the model proposes possible outcomes, a program ranks tests by expected information gain) beat the model choosing tests by itself, random choice and a fixed subset on three clinical tabular datasets with GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o. Implicit model selection favoured globally popular tests and did not adapt to the case. A KL stopping rule cut tests by about 50%.
agent_test: On a circuit diagnosis task, compare a plain 'what next?' prompt with a code step that ranks probes by entropy over the current candidate set; count probes to isolate the fault.

claim: A structured panel around one model (kept differential, a challenger who looks for disconfirming evidence, a test chooser, a cost steward) gave o3 the same accuracy at about 70% lower cost (79.9% at $2,397 vs 78.6% at $7,850) on 304 interactive NEJM cases, and 85.5% with ensembling. Case review showed the bare model anchoring. No per-role ablation was reported, so which part causes the gain is not known.
agent_test: Ablate the challenger step alone and the hypothesis-tracking step alone on a diagnosis benchmark at equal tokens.

claim: With 2025-26 models, intrinsic self-correction gives little. Reasoning models gain little from added correction methods and pay a time cost (CorrectBench). The strongest of three models (94%) corrected 16.7% of its errors and a location hint made all three worse (Li 2026, preprint, n=346 errors). External checks give more than same-model review.
schema_part: G (no same-model self-review as a check)
agent_test: On a diagnosis task with a reasoning model, compare an added same-model review step with a code check of the same cost.

claim: Execution-grounded input is cheap and strong for fault localisation: an LLM estimating the executed trace from one real failure log reached trace F1 about 90% and Hit@3 81% on 785 industrial cases with 93% fewer tokens than the latest LLM-guided method. Trained debugger imitators predict next state above 90% but need training. Prompted simulation of execution remains weaker than real execution (earlier evidence b20-b22); a 2025 test with current models was not found.
agent_test: Compare real tool output versus model-predicted output as the observation for the same hypothesis-test step, equal tokens.

claim: No published LLM test was found for: fault-model choice (weak vs strong fault), GDE-style entropy probe selection on circuits, or models handling superset diagnoses after a measurement. These stay open design questions.
agent_test: Build the three small tests on circuits with known diagnoses.
